::: {.why}
The deflated Sharpe corrects one number; the reality check tests the whole set at once, and the distinction between the two nulls is the part people get wrong.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State White's null hypothesis precisely, and say why it is stronger than testing each strategy separately.
- Run the reality check and the superior predictive ability test on a set of your own strategies and report both p-values.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read White's Reality Check paper as far as the statement of the null and the bootstrap procedure. The null is that the best strategy in the set has no expected outperformance over the benchmark, which is a joint statement rather than 200 separate ones.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Run it with arch: take 50 moving-average variants on SPY, form the loss differentials against a buy-and-hold benchmark, and apply the SPA test from arch.bootstrap. Report the consistent and lower p-values. You are calling a stationary bootstrap you have not built yet, which is next week's work; today the resampling is a black box.
:::
:::

- [White (2000) — A Reality Check for Data Snooping](https://users.ssc.wisc.edu/~bhansen/718/White2000.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

State White's null in one sentence, and say why rejecting it is a stronger claim than a single strategy having a significant Sharpe.
